During the '''1991–92 Serie A''', under the guidance of [[Fabio Capello]], [[AC Milan|Milan]] completed a remarkable unbeaten season, a run that eventually totalled 58 games. They finished eight points ahead of Serie A runners-up [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]. However, it was a disappointing season for [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], who could only manage an eighth-place finish, meaning that 1992–93 would bring no European action for them — something which had been a rare occurrence over the last three decades. Defending champions [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] finished sixth and their last chance of European action for the following season was lost when they were beaten by the [[Spain|Spanish]] champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the final of the [[European Cup]]. [[AS Bari|Bari]], [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]] (the 1985 champions), [[US Cremonese|Cremonese]] and [[Ascoli Calcio 1898 FC|Ascoli]] were all relegated.

==Teams==
[[US Foggia|Foggia]], [[Hellas Verona]], [[US Cremonese|Cremonese]] and [[Ascoli Calcio|Ascoli]] had been promoted from [[Serie B]].
